name: What local considerations should I be aware of regarding property taxes and insurance in South Florida?

mainEntity.name: What local considerations should I be aware of regarding property taxes and insurance in South Florida?

acceptedAnswer.text: Property taxes and insurance are significant local considerations when moving to South Florida. Property taxes are assessed by individual counties (Miami-Dade, Broward, Palm Beach, Collier, Orange) and are based on the assessed value of your home, which can change annually. Homestead exemptions are available for primary residents and can help reduce your taxable value. Homeowners insurance, particularly windstorm and flood insurance, is crucial due to the region's climate and coastal location, and premiums can be substantial. For example, properties in designated flood zones will require flood insurance. It's important to obtain insurance quotes early in your home search to get a realistic understanding of your total monthly housing expenses.
acceptedAnswer.description: Property taxes are county-assessed and homeowners insurance, including flood and windstorm, is crucial in South Florida; homestead exemptions can reduce taxes for primary residents.
